children: Royal Caribbean (RCL) could be opening a much larger competitive advantage with its $3 billion investment in Sandals Resorts, according to Citi Research, which placed the cruise operator on a 90-day positive Catalyst Watch. Analyst James Hardiman argues the transaction could push Royal Caribbean beyond the traditional cruise model and create a vacation ecosystem that rivals may struggle to match.
Royal Caribbean confirmed Wednesday that it invested about $3 billion for a 50% stake in Sandals and Beaches, implying an enterprise value of roughly $6 billion.
At first glance, the deal looks like a straightforward expansion into all-inclusive resorts.

If, and when, the vacation choice becomes less about one ship vs. another and more about one vacation ecosystem vs. another, this choice becomes more obvious as RCL builds out a portfolio the breadth of which dwarfs the competition, he wrote.
That portfolio already extends beyond ships.

Royal Caribbean has been expanding private destinations such as Perfect Day at CocoCay, Royal Beach Club Nassau and Royal Beach Club Cozumel, while also building exposure to river cruising. Sandals and Beaches now add established all-inclusive resort brands to that mix.
Hardiman believes the more important question is not simply what Royal Caribbean can do for Sandals, but what Sandals can do for Royal Caribbean.

Adding the resorts to Royal Caribbean's growing land-based portfolio increasingly creates a Caribbean ecosystem that does not exist elsewhere in the cruise industry and has not existed in the history of the travel industry, according to Hardiman.
For Royal Caribbean investors, the key opportunity is cross-selling.

A unified ecosystem spanning ships, resorts, private destinations, beach clubs and river cruises could allow Royal Caribbean to keep customers spending within its portfolio across more types of vacations.
That could deepen loyalty, improve customer lifetime value and differentiate Royal Caribbean from Carnival and Norwegian Cruise Line.
The key things to watch are integration, loyalty-program expansion and whether Sandals meaningfully increases repeat bookings across the broader Royal Caribbean ecosystem.
If those synergies materialize, Citi's argument is that Royal Caribbean may increasingly compete on the breadth of its entire vacation platform rather than on cruise ships alone.

title: Royal Caribbean Gets Bullish Citi Call on Sandals Bet
